content.value_statement: Long agent sessions lose important details when context is compressed too aggressively. This skill provides structured summaries and probe-based checks that preserve decisions, files, risks, and next actions.
actual_capabilities: Explains anchored iterative summarization for long agent sessions.
Defines mandatory summary sections for intent, files, decisions, state, and next steps.
Compares anchored, opaque, and regenerative compression methods.
Provides probe types for recall, artifact tracking, continuation, and decisions.
Includes a Python evaluator for scoring compressed context responses.
Describes common failure modes such as lost file paths and hallucinated details.
limitations: The evaluator uses heuristic scoring unless users connect a real LLM judge.
The benchmark figures are reference guidance, not universal guarantees.
The skill does not automatically compress live chat history by itself.
Users must validate compressed summaries before deleting original context.

use_cases.title: Preserve Coding Session State
use_cases.description: Create summaries that keep file changes, test status, decisions, and next actions available after compaction.

use_cases.title: Evaluate Compression Quality
use_cases.description: Build probe sets that test whether important facts survived context compression.

use_cases.title: Prepare Durable Handoffs
use_cases.description: Turn long investigations into structured handoff notes for another agent or teammate.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize a Session
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a structured compact summary.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the context-compression skill to summarize this session. Preserve intent, files changed, decisions, current state, risks, and next steps.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Compression Strategy
prompt_templates.scenario: Select the right approach for a session profile.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare anchored iterative, opaque, and regenerative compression for this project. Recommend one method and explain the trade-offs.

prompt_templates.title: Create Evaluation Probes
prompt_templates.scenario: Test whether a compressed summary retained critical details.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design probe questions for this compressed context. Cover recall, artifact tracking, continuation, decisions, completeness, and instruction following.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Compression Drift
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of repeated compaction cycles.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these compression cycles for drift. Identify lost identifiers, changed decisions, hallucinated facts, and weak probe coverage.

output_examples.input: A long debugging session is near the context limit.
output_examples.output: A structured handoff summary lists the original error, root cause, examined files, modified files, test status, risks, and next actions.

output_examples.input: A team needs to compare two summary methods.
output_examples.output: The skill produces probe questions and scoring guidance that reveal which method preserves artifact trails and decision rationale better.

output_examples.input: An agent forgot which files it changed after compaction.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends a dedicated artifact section and separate file-state tracking to reduce repeated re-reading.

best_practices: Keep file paths, identifiers, errors, and decisions in dedicated summary sections.
Merge only newly truncated content during repeated compression cycles.
Use probes to test the exact facts needed for task continuation.
anti_patterns: Do not optimize only for the smallest possible context size.
Do not compress tool schemas, API contracts, or required parameter names.
Do not delete original context until the summary is checked against source material.

faq.question: Does this skill automatically reduce token usage?
faq.answer: No. It provides strategy, templates, and evaluation guidance for building better compression workflows.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What compression method does it prefer?
faq.answer: It generally favors anchored iterative summarization when file tracking and decision history matter.

faq.question: Can it evaluate compressed summaries?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes probe categories and a Python evaluator that can score responses against rubrics.

faq.question: Is opaque compression always worse?
faq.answer: No. It can be useful when maximum compression matters and re-fetching costs are low.

faq.question: What should users preserve most carefully?
faq.answer: Preserve file paths, function names, decisions, errors, constraints, test status, and remaining actions.
